intent: To illustrate how the high concentration of the population in urban areas creates a dense ecosystem for startups and introduces demographics as a key factor.

units.meaning: The urban population share is 92%, indicating that the vast majority of the measured population lives in urban areas.
accepted_routes: 92% of Israelis live in urban areas
urban residents make up approximately 92% of the total
units.visual_evidence_rule: A central donut/percentage mark or label must visibly show 92% as the urban share, with the urban segment dominating the composition.
units.temporal_anchor: opening narration clause about 92% of Israelis living in urban areas
units.reviewer_question: Must the exact 92% value be stated or labeled, or is a visual majority/donut sufficient?

units.meaning: Demographics is introduced as another key factor for talent/startup ecosystems, with no numeric demographic value in the table.
accepted_routes: Demographics is another important talent factor
The video then introduces demographics as key
Demographics is highlighted as overlooked but important
units.visual_evidence_rule: A title, callout, or narration transition must mention demographics as a key factor; no demographic data need be plotted.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video include the demographic transition even though the data table has no demographic value?

optional_valid: Showing the relative_value 0.92 as an alternative notation for the 92% share.
Using a donut chart because the table contains a single share/composition datum.
The single x_px value can support a one-slice or donut layout rather than a time-series axis.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims that urban concentration creates startup density or surrounds startups with customers/partners/competitors.
The northern-half geographic concentration mentioned only in narration, since it is not in the table.
Any absolute population counts, city-level data, or startup counts.
Any demographic percentages, demographic trends, or causal effects of demographics.
Any time-series change, year-over-year comparison, or multiple data series.
notes: Only one numeric datum is available: 92% urban share (relative_value 0.92). U5 is an intent-driven qualitative transition with no numeric table basis.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
